display.title: Episode 340: The Storyteller, Chapter 3 (Rosh Chodesh Elul)
display.summary_short: Elul and the King in the Field, the Hakochainik march, Shema with a first-grade class, Rabbi Yehuda hears of a rich man who pays for Baal Shem Tov stories, and the first shofar of Elul.
display.summary_long: Broadcast a few days before Rosh Chodesh Elul 5748. Uncle Yossi explains why Elul should make us cry 'Oy gevald!': using the Alter Rebbe's parable from Likkutei Torah, Hashem in Elul is like a king who comes out to the fields, greets everyone with a smile and grants their requests, and at the top of every list is 'We want Moshiach now.' After the Hakochainik march to 'Sheyibaneh Beis HaMikdash', the story continues: for months Rabbi Yehuda tells stories for pennies, until a kind hotel owner, Reb Avraham, feeds him and tells him of a wealthy merchant, Reb Yitzchak, who pays huge sums for any new story about the Baal Shem Tov. A first-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school recites the Shema, and Rabbi Yehuda sets off for the mansion saying Tehillim. A young listener's letter about the Tzivos Hashem club is read, and Uncle Yossi explains that the shofar will be blown every weekday morning in Elul to prepare for Rosh Hashanah. Candle-lighting time and the Dial-a-Jewish-Story line close the show.
display.lesson: In Elul Hashem is close like a king in the field, so ask Him for what matters most; and never give up, because help can come from where you least expect it.
